title: TSMC says unable to keep pace with AI boom despite fivefold expansion
gist: TSMC is building 25 fabs and packaging facilities this year (13 in Taiwan) versus a historical pace of 5-6 per year, and has raised its 2026 capex guidance twice in six months (+~90% from its prior estimate), yet deputy COO Cliff Hou says the company still cannot keep up with AI demand; MediaTek, Nvidia, Hon Hai and Unimicron executives at the same event described compounding capacity and substrate shortages and a strategic shift toward 'made with Taiwan' global manufacturing.

themes.theme: TSMC's unprecedented capacity build-out still falling short

insights.claim: TSMC deputy cochief operating officer Cliff Hou said the company is building 25 chip manufacturing fabs and advanced packaging facilities worldwide this year, including 13 plants in Taiwan, versus a historical pace of five or six factories per year, yet is still unable to keep up with AI demand.
insights.speaker: Cliff Hou (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A fivefold jump in simultaneous fab/packaging construction (25 vs. historical 5-6) that still trails demand is a strong leading indicator that AI-driven capex intensity for TSMC and its equipment suppliers (ASML, Applied Materials, etc.) is not near a plateau.
insights.quote: Compared with the pattern 30 years ago, we have never seen the demand increase that much, that frequency of changes
insights.locator: opening paragraphs, Cliff Hou at CEO Summit fireside chat

insights.claim: TSMC has twice raised its capital expenditure budget for this year within six months, expanding its overall outlays by about 90 percent from an estimate made at the end of last year.
insights.speaker: Cliff Hou (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A ~90% upward capex revision within six months is an unusually large and fast guidance change, signaling either severe prior demand underestimation or a rapidly escalating AI arms race among customers — a key data point for modeling TSMC's near-term margin and depreciation trajectory.

insights.claim: Hou said exponential AI scaling relies on advancing computational capacity and optimizing power efficiency, and that customers are showing much faster demand shifts for advanced process, packaging and system performance than ever before.
insights.speaker: Cliff Hou (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Faster customer demand-shift cycles imply TSMC and its ecosystem need shorter qualification and ramp timelines just to keep pace, raising execution risk if any single node or packaging transition slips.

insights.claim: Hou said the whole AI supply chain, not just TSMC, is doubling down on capacity expansion to solve supply issues.
insights.speaker: Cliff Hou (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A supply-chain-wide capacity race (not isolated to TSMC) raises the risk of an eventual overbuild/glut if AI demand growth decelerates, a scenario worth monitoring for capex-cycle timing.

themes.theme: MediaTek's capacity commitments and Nvidia partnership

insights.claim: MediaTek CEO Rick Tsai said the company has asked TSMC and ASE Technology Holding for more capacity from next year through 2029 to address supply constraints, and has secured stable chip supply from TSMC.
insights.speaker: Rick Tsai (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A multi-year (through 2029) capacity request from a top fabless customer confirms demand visibility extends well past the current cycle, supporting long-duration capex commitments by TSMC/ASE.

insights.claim: Nvidia announced a US$3.5 billion investment in MediaTek's corporate bonds, which Tsai called a vote of confidence, and Tsai said the companies' latest strategic collaboration using Nvidia's NVLink Fusion technology (for high-speed server-rack connections) would positively impact MediaTek's AI custom chip business.
insights.speaker: Rick Tsai (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A $3.5 billion bond investment plus NVLink Fusion integration signals Nvidia is deepening financial and technical ties with MediaTek's custom AI silicon business, a competitive signal for other ASIC/custom-chip players (Broadcom, Marvell) to watch.
insights.locator: paragraph on Nvidia's $3.5 billion bond investment

insights.claim: MediaTek maintained its AI custom chip revenue target of US$2 billion for the next quarter.
insights.speaker: Rick Tsai (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A reaffirmed $2 billion quarterly AI custom-chip revenue target is a concrete near-term benchmark for tracking MediaTek's AI diversification away from smartphone chips.

themes.theme: 'Made with Taiwan' — the shift to distributed global manufacturing

insights.claim: Hon Hai Precision Industry chairman Young Liu said Taiwan's technology sector should shift from concentrating production at home to a 'made with Taiwan' model, as surging AI demand and geopolitical pressures reshape global supply chains.
insights.speaker: Young Liu (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A shift from 'made in Taiwan' to 'made with Taiwan' signals accelerating geographic diversification of Taiwanese manufacturing (echoing TSMC's Arizona/Japan expansions), which investors should track as a hedge against Taiwan Strait geopolitical risk but also as a margin/cost variable.
insights.quote: We all have to think about how to make with Taiwan, not in Taiwan
insights.locator: quote from Young Liu on manufacturing strategy

insights.claim: MediaTek's Rick Tsai said Taiwan's advantage lies in combining technological capability, flexibility and speed, and that Taiwan's supply chain is already 'a global Taiwan' rather than a purely domestic operation, with local companies continuing to expand internationally and partner overseas where they lack capabilities.
insights.speaker: Rick Tsai (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Framing Taiwan's supply chain as already globally distributed (not just Taiwan-based) softens the pure geographic-concentration risk narrative for investors, suggesting resilience through international partnerships rather than single-island dependence.
insights.locator: paragraph on Taiwan's 'global Taiwan' supply chain

insights.claim: Unimicron Technology chairman Chien Shan-chieh said AI demand has intensified a shortage of semiconductor substrates while creating requirements for larger and more complex designs, and that the industry depends on suppliers of critical tools and materials, many of them small and medium-sized Japanese companies facing their own capacity pressures.
insights.speaker: Chien Shan-chieh (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Identifying small/mid-size Japanese substrate and materials suppliers as a capacity chokepoint highlights an under-the-radar bottleneck upstream of TSMC/ASE that could constrain the entire advanced-packaging supply chain regardless of foundry capex.
